behavior: Enumerate every vertex pair in lexicographic order with zero less than or equal to i less than j less than count.
Read both vertices concurrently from the two RAM ports.
Form signed 33-bit coordinate differences, calculate two 66-bit squares, and add them with a 67-bit guard result.
Update the maximum only on a strictly greater distance so equal maxima retain the first lexicographic pair.
Issue one pair per clock and complete one nontrivial scan in pair-count plus four clocks.
constraints: Coordinates are signed Q16.16 and the distance result has 32 fractional bits.
Vertex counts above 1024 fail before any RAM read.
The RAM ports return simultaneous one-cycle valid responses for each request.
The upstream controller must wait while busy is asserted.
corner_cases: Zero vertices return empty with distance zero and indices zero,zero.
One vertex returns distance zero and indices zero,zero.
Two vertices evaluate exactly one pair.
All identical vertices retain pair zero,one even though every distance is zero.
Opposite signed coordinate extremes fit the 66-bit output without saturation.
verification_cases: Check zero, one, and two vertex inputs.
Check a rectangle with tied diagonals and a signed-coordinate five-vertex polygon.
Check identical points, full signed coordinate span, and an input count above capacity.
Check all 258840 pairs of the 720-vertex stage-one baseline at one issued pair per clock.
Check pair count, latency formula, pulse width, buffer selection, and busy-start rejection.
